description: Storskog is a scattering of homesteads along a great northern river, three days upstream from the coast, surrounded by forest that seems to have no end. Every winter the timber companies from the coastal sawmills send crews to fell trees on land they bought cheaply from the farmers, hauling logs down to the river ice to wait for the spring flood. Beyond the last farm there are only marshes, ridges and the camps.
seasonNotes: December, the depth of winter. The sun barely clears the ridges for a few hours around noon and the rest is blue twilight and dark. Snow lies thigh-deep in the forest and the river is frozen hard enough for horses. The cold reaches thirty degrees below on still nights, and trees crack like gunshots in the frost. Felling and hauling go on by daylight; the crews come down to the chapel for Christmas only if the weather allows.
travel: From Uppsala in December: post coach to Gävle (about 1 day), post sleigh up the coast to Härnösand (about 3 days), then sleigh on the river ice via Sollefteå to Storskog (about 2 days), roughly six days in all; in the open season (May-October) rail to Stockholm, coastal steamer to Härnösand, river steamer to Sollefteå and cart to Storskog, about five days.

geography.realAnalogue: Junsele (Ångermanälven valley above Sollefteå, inland Ångermanland)
geography.parish: Storskog (a chapel congregation under a larger upriver parish; the parish itself is fictional)
knownFor: Timber: the coastal sawmills buy up the valley's forest and float its logs down the Ångermanälven each spring flood.
The hunger years of 1867-68, when Norrland farmers ate bark bread and some farms were left empty.
Settlers clearing new homesteads on crown forest land, with years free of tax.
Forests so wide and thinly peopled that the crown sheriff covers them mostly by sleigh in winter.

authorities.police: The kronolänsman of the Storskog district sits at Sollefteå, about 60 km away. He covers a vast forest district and reaches Storskog only on sleigh rounds in winter or when sent for. In practice the village depends on its own church-warden and the logging boss.
authorities.court: Häradsrätt for inland Ångermanland at Sollefteå, with a judge and twelve lay assessors. It sits in fixed sessions and extra sittings in winter, when the sleigh roads are best for witnesses. Appeals go to Härnösand.
authorities.doctor: The provincial doctor for inland Ångermanland lives at Sollefteå. He is a day or more away and often has to be fetched by sleigh. He signs the death certificates and explains camp injuries, frostbite and fevers in natural terms.
authorities.post: The post comes up the valley by farm-to-farm relay, about once a week in winter and less often in thaw or break-up. Letters are left at the Ferry Posting Farm and sent on from the chapel.
authorities.telegraph: The nearest office is at Härnösand on the Norrland coast line, about 150 km away. The valley has no wire, so a telegram has to be carried up by sleigh or river boat, taking two to three days.
authorities.bank: Hernösands Enskilda Bank at Härnösand finances the timber firms and sawmills. A parish savings bank at Sollefteå serves small farmers.
authorities.newspaper: Hernösands-Posten, from Härnösand. It prints timber prices, court news and notices of the logging firms, and arrives days or weeks late.

routes.name: Winter road: coach and sleigh via Gävle, Härnösand and the river ice

legs.duration: about one long day (c. 100 km) with changes of horses at the posting stations
legs.cost: about 8 riksdaler by post coach or 20-25 by hired carriage, food at the stations extra
legs.schedule: post coach a few days a week; hired carriage any day
legs.notes: The Uppsala-Gävle railway is only being built and opens in 1874, so the road is the only way. In December, snow may already make a sleigh necessary on the northern stretch.

legs.duration: about three days (c. 300 km) by post sleigh, changing horses at each posting farm
legs.cost: about 25-30 riksdaler for a hired sleigh with posting fees; lodging and food extra
legs.schedule: post sleigh a few times a week; hired sleighs on demand, with horses ordered ahead at the posting farms
legs.notes: The coastal steamers are stopped by ice and the sleigh is the only way. Posting farms at Hudiksvall and Sundsvall are the main stops, and fresh snow can slow the road to a walk.

legs.duration: about one day (c. 90 km) by road and river ice
legs.cost: about 6-8 riksdaler for a hired sleigh and driver
legs.schedule: on demand; ask at the posting farm or the livery
legs.notes: River steamers are laid up and the ice road is safe for horses from Advent until the end of March. Wind-swept stretches and open water near rapids and inflows are dangerous at dusk.

legs.duration: about one long day (c. 60 km) upriver on the ice and forest road
legs.cost: about 4-5 riksdaler for a hired sleigh; the ferryman's horses can be hired for the last stretch
legs.schedule: on demand; log haulers also come down with empty sleighs
legs.notes: Dark falls early in December, so travellers lodge on the way at a farm or a logging camp. A telegram or letter sent ahead may arrive after the traveller.

routes.name: Open-water route: railway to Stockholm, coastal steamer and river steamer

legs.duration: about two and a half hours
legs.notes: Via Knivsta, Märsta and Rotebro. Runs all year, but the steamer connection is only in the open season.

legs.duration: about two days at sea, calling at Östhammar, Gävle, Hudiksvall and Sundsvall
legs.cost: about 20 riksdaler second class, meals extra
legs.schedule: once or twice a week in season
legs.notes: Ice stops the route in winter. Sailings may be delayed by autumn gales.

legs.schedule: a few sailings a week in the open season
legs.notes: The small river steamer calls at Kramfors and landings on the way. Low water in late summer can strand it at the shallows.

legs.duration: about one long day (c. 60 km) by farm road and river track
legs.cost: about 3-4 riksdaler for a hired cart and driver
legs.schedule: on demand; the ferryman keeps horses at the posting farm
legs.notes: The road is poor and muddy in autumn rain. Mosquitoes and midges are bad in summer near the marshes.

journey.journeyScene: The post coach rattles north out of Uppsala through flat farmland. By Gävle the snow is thicker and the sea smoky with ice. Then the hired sleigh runs for days up the coast through Hälsingland, with bells on the harness, steaming horses and posting farms where the hostler wakes at dawn to harness fresh ones. Beyond Härnösand the way turns up the frozen river between walls of black spruce, and the daylight shrinks to a few grey hours. Lamps glow only at far-apart farms and logging camps, and you pass haulers with groaning log sleighs who seem to say little and look hard at strangers..

publicFacts: Most of the forest round Storskog was sold to a coastal sawmill company in the 1860s for a fraction of its worth; many farmers regret it.
The famine winter of 1867 is remembered here; people ate bark bread and two families died out.
Logging crews come up from the coast and from Finland each winter and leave with the spring flood.
The nearest priest serves the chapel only once a month; on other Sundays a lay reader holds the service.
The posting farm at the ferry keeps horses for travellers and sells brännvin, although it has no licence.
The river ice is reckoned safe for horses from Advent until the end of March.
Settlers have been clearing new homesteads on the crown forest land, where the government gives them years free of tax.

places.name: The Camp at Svartberget
places.ownerRole: the logging boss, who runs the camp for a timber company
places.description: The camp is a pair of low log huts half buried in snow at the foot of a black ridge, smoke rising straight up in the frozen air. Inside, a long fire burns down the middle and wet socks and mittens steam on poles above it. Outside the horses stand blanketed, breath freezing in their manes, beside sleds loaded with logs. The ring of axes and the shouts of the fellers carry a long way in the silence.

affordances.name: Log hut 1
affordances.description: A koja of unbarked logs, sleeping benches along the walls, a smoke hole in the roof and frost on the inside of the door.

contains.name: Long fire
contains.description: The long fire of the hut, kept burning all night.

affordances.name: Log hut 2

affordances.name: Horse shelter

affordances.name: Tool store
affordances.description: Axes, bow saws, chains and sled runners.

places.name: Nybygget
places.ownerRole: a settler family clearing new land
places.description: A new settler's cabin stands in a raw clearing of stumps, its logs still pale, with snow banked to the windowsills for warmth. A single cow lows in the byre built against the house. The family burns birch, and the smell carries far through the trees. Ski tracks lead off in three directions into the forest.

affordances.name: Cottage room
affordances.description: One room: hearth, a box bed for the parents, a pull-out bench for the children, a table under the window.

contains.name: Hearth
contains.description: The hearth, smoke-blackened, a pot simmering.

contains.name: Clothes chest
contains.description: The family's one chest for Sunday clothes and papers.

affordances.name: Byre
affordances.description: A byre built against the cottage for one cow and a few sheep.

affordances.name: Earth cellar
affordances.description: A turf-roofed earth cellar for potatoes.

affordances.name: Well
affordances.description: A shallow well or a spring-fed pit with a bucket.

affordances.name: Potato patch
affordances.description: A stony patch of potatoes, kale and tobacco plants.

places.name: Storskog Farm
places.ownerRole: the farming family of Storskog, the oldest in the valley
places.description: The old farm stands on a rise above the river, a long two-storey house with outbuildings forming a closed yard against the wind. Lamps burn in the windows through the short day. The farm's women are baking flatbread for Christmas, and the warmth and smell drift out whenever the door opens. Below, the river is a white road through the forest.

affordances.name: Farmyard
affordances.description: The yard between the buildings, trodden mud and a woodpile.

affordances.name: Main room
affordances.description: The everyday room: open hearth, long table, wall beds and the loom in the corner.

contains.name: Open hearth
contains.description: The whitewashed corner hearth with its iron pot-hook.

affordances.name: Cowshed
affordances.description: A low dark byre, warm with cattle breath.

affordances.name: Stable
affordances.description: A stable for the farm horse or horses.

affordances.name: Barn
affordances.description: A timber barn for the harvest.

contains.name: Hayloft
contains.description: The hay store over the barn floor, reached by a ladder.

affordances.name: Threshing barn
affordances.description: A threshing barn (loge) where the grain is threshed with flails through the autumn.

affordances.name: Root cellar
affordances.description: A root cellar dug into the slope, holding potatoes, turnips and the milk.

affordances.name: Well
affordances.description: A well with a sweep pole and a wooden bucket.

affordances.name: Bathhouse
affordances.description: A small log bastu with a stone oven, also used for drying malt and flax.

places.name: The Ferry Posting Farm
places.ownerRole: the ferryman, who keeps the posting farm at the ferry
places.description: At the ferry crossing a posting farm keeps a fire and a few horses, with a single guest room up a ladder. In winter the ferry is drawn up on the bank and the road runs straight across the ice, marked with spruce branches. The taproom is the farm's kitchen, where loggers sit with their caps on. A wolfskin is nailed to the barn wall.

affordances.name: Taproom
affordances.description: The public room: benches, a long scrubbed table, a tiled stove and the day's travellers.

affordances.name: Kitchen
affordances.description: A smoky kitchen with an open hearth, copper pans and a bread rack under the ceiling.

affordances.name: Guest room
affordances.description: A narrow room with a bed, a washstand and a window onto the yard.

contains.name: Travelling chest
contains.description: A painted chest at the foot of the bed for a guest's things.

affordances.name: Posting stable
affordances.description: Stalls for the posting horses, harness on pegs, the smell of hay and dung.

affordances.name: Cellar
affordances.description: A stone cellar for ale, potatoes and the inn's barrels.

places.name: Storskog Chapel
places.ownerRole: the verger (klockare), who keeps the chapel between the comminister's visits
places.description: A small wooden chapel, tarred black and roofed with shingles, stands on a knoll with a few snow-covered graves around it. The bell hangs in an open frame and its rope is stiff with frost. Inside, the pews are rough planks and the altar painting is the work of a travelling painter. On the Sundays without a priest the lay reader's voice sounds thin in the cold.

affordances.name: Sacristy
affordances.description: A small vaulted room off the chancel where the vicar robes.

contains.name: Vestment cupboard
contains.description: A tall cupboard of chasubles, the surplice and spare altar candles.

contains.name: Parish chest
contains.description: An ancient iron-banded chest with three locks for the communion silver and old deeds.

affordances.name: Bell tower
affordances.description: Steep ladders up to the bells, bird droppings on the beams, wind through the louvres.

affordances.name: Church loft
affordances.description: The dusty space above the vaults, full of broken pews and old hatchments.

places.name: The Cottage by the Bog
places.ownerRole: the wise woman of the valley
places.description: A tiny cottage stands where the forest meets a frozen bog, so snowed in that only the chimney and a trodden path mark it. Inside, the air is thick with smoke and the smell of tar salve and dried yarrow. Reindeer hides cover the bench. The old woman who lives there sets bones for the loggers, who pay her in coffee and salt pork.

affordances.name: Cottage room
affordances.description: A single low room, dim and smelling of smoke and herbs.

contains.name: Hearth
contains.description: A hearth with a brew always going.

affordances.name: Herb store
affordances.description: Bunches of drying herbs from the rafters, jars of salve and dried roots.

contains.name: Remedy cupboard
contains.description: A small cupboard of bottles, wrapped in rag and labelled in a crabbed hand.

contains.name: Small box
contains.description: A small wooden box kept on a high shelf.

affordances.name: Herb garden
affordances.description: A fenced garden of medicinal plants.

affordances.name: Earth cellar
affordances.description: A small earth cellar.

affordances.name: Spring
affordances.description: A spring-fed well with a cup on a string.

places.name: The Camp Smith
places.description: A rough forge in a lean-to at the foot of the river bank, where the company smith mends chains, sled runners and horseshoes for the camps. The fire's glow is the only colour in the blue noon twilight. Iron frozen to the anvil has to be warmed before it will move. Horses wait in a row to have studs fitted for the ice.

affordances.name: Forge
affordances.description: The hearth and bellows, the anvil on its stump, the quench trough.

affordances.name: Workshop
affordances.description: The bench and racks of tongs, hammers and half-finished work.

affordances.name: Coal shed
affordances.description: A shed of charcoal and bar iron from the works.

affordances.name: Smith's cottage
affordances.description: The smith's one-room cottage across the yard.

contains.name: Smith's chest
contains.description: The smith's own chest of papers and good clothes.
